target: Kami membatalkan piknik karena hujan turun deras sekali.
english: We canceled the picnic because the rain came down very hard.

target: Dia terlambat ke rapat karena bus kota datang sangat lambat.
english: He was late to the meeting because the city bus came very slowly.

target: Saya memilih kereta karena tiket pesawat mahal sekali bulan ini.
english: I chose the train because plane tickets are very expensive this month.

target: Anak saya senang sekali karena besok kami pergi ke kebun binatang.
english: My child is very happy because tomorrow we are going to the zoo.

target: Kami pindah ke kota ini karena istri saya dapat pekerjaan baru.
english: We moved to this city because my wife got a new job.

target: Restoran itu selalu penuh karena masakannya enak dan murah.
english: That restaurant is always full because its food is tasty and cheap.

target: Karena jalan macet, kami berangkat lebih pagi dari biasanya.
english: Because the roads are jammed, we leave earlier than usual.
grammar: karena = because; the reason clause can come first: Karena hujan, kami pulang = Because it rained, we went home.

target: Ibu menutup semua jendela karena angin sore ini kencang sekali.
english: Mom is closing all the windows because the wind this afternoon is very strong.

target: Saya minum teh jahe hangat karena tenggorokan saya sakit sejak kemarin.
english: I am drinking warm ginger tea because my throat has hurt since yesterday.

target: Kami memesan kamar dengan sarapan karena harganya hampir sama saja.
english: We booked a room with breakfast because the price is almost the same anyway.

target: Dia belajar bahasa Indonesia karena tahun depan dia pindah ke Jakarta.
english: She is studying Indonesian because next year she is moving to Jakarta.

target: Ayah tidur lebih awal karena besok dia harus berangkat jam lima.
english: Dad is going to bed earlier because tomorrow he has to leave at five.
grammar: Clock times use jam + number: jam lima = five o'clock, jam lima pagi = five in the morning.

target: Kami makan di rumah karena semua restoran dekat sini sudah tutup.
english: We are eating at home because all the restaurants near here are already closed.

target: Saya selalu membawa payung karena musim hujan sudah mulai.
english: I always carry an umbrella because the rainy season has already started.

target: Saya pulang dulu, soalnya besok saya harus bangun pagi sekali.
english: I'm heading home now, because tomorrow I have to get up very early.
grammar: soalnya = spoken 'because', after the statement: ..., soalnya sudah malam = ..., because it's late. In writing: karena.

target: Kita lewat jalan belakang saja, soalnya jalan besar pasti macet.
english: Let's just take the back road, because the main road is definitely jammed.

target: Jangan pesan sup itu, soalnya porsinya kecil dan harganya mahal.
english: Don't order that soup, because the portion is small and the price is high.

target: Aku tidak ikut menonton film, soalnya dompetku ketinggalan di rumah.
english: I'm not coming along to watch the movie, because my wallet got left at home.
grammar: ketinggalan = got left behind by accident: dompetku ketinggalan = my wallet got left behind.

target: Kami duduk di dalam saja, soalnya di luar panas sekali.
english: We'll just sit inside, because it's very hot outside.

target: Dia tidak masuk kerja hari ini, soalnya anaknya sakit.
english: She isn't coming to work today, because her child is sick.
grammar: soalnya gives the excuse after the fact: Dia tidak masuk, soalnya anaknya sakit = ..., because her child is sick.

target: Beli tiketnya sekarang saja, soalnya kursi kereta cepat habis.
english: Just buy the tickets now, because train seats run out fast.

target: Saya jarang memasak ikan, soalnya anak saya tidak suka baunya.
english: I rarely cook fish, because my child doesn't like the smell.

target: Hujan turun deras sekali, jadi kami menunggu di dalam kafe.
english: The rain came down very hard, so we waited inside a cafe.
grammar: jadi = so; it starts the result: Hujan deras, jadi kami menunggu = It rained hard, so we waited.

target: Baterai ponsel saya habis, jadi saya tidak bisa menelepon kamu.
english: My phone battery ran out, so I couldn't call you.

target: Besok hari libur, jadi kita bisa sarapan pelan-pelan di rumah.
english: Tomorrow is a holiday, so we can have a slow breakfast at home.
grammar: Doubling slows it down: pelan-pelan = slowly, sarapan pelan-pelan = a leisurely breakfast.

target: Kopinya sudah habis, jadi saya memesan segelas teh manis.
english: The coffee was already gone, so I ordered a glass of sweet tea.

target: Hotel itu penuh, jadi kami mencari penginapan lain dekat stasiun.
english: That hotel was full, so we looked for other lodging near the station.

target: Rapatnya selesai lebih cepat, jadi saya bisa pulang sebelum gelap.
english: The meeting finished early, so I can go home before dark.

target: Adik saya sudah bisa memasak, jadi ibu bisa istirahat lebih lama.
english: My younger sibling can already cook, so Mom can rest longer.

target: Toko roti itu tutup hari Senin, jadi kita datang besok saja.
english: That bakery is closed on Mondays, so let's just come tomorrow.
grammar: This jadi = 'so'. jadi also means 'become' (jadi guru = become a teacher) — context decides.

target: Saya lupa membawa dompet, jadi teman saya membayar makan siang.
english: I forgot to bring my wallet, so my friend paid for lunch.

target: Cuaca sore ini cerah, jadi kami jalan kaki ke taman.
english: The weather this afternoon is clear, so we're walking to the park.

target: Tiket pesawat sedang murah, jadi kami memesan untuk bulan Desember.
english: Plane tickets are cheap right now, so we booked for December.

target: Kamar ini kecil, jadi kami menaruh lemari di ruang keluarga.
english: This room is small, so we put the wardrobe in the family room.

target: Saya menulis daftar belanja supaya tidak lupa di toko.
english: I write a shopping list so that I don't forget things at the store.
grammar: supaya = so that (a goal): supaya tidak lupa = so that I don't forget. No extra word for 'that'.

target: Kami berangkat pagi sekali supaya jalan tol masih kosong.
english: We leave very early so that the toll road is still empty.

target: Tolong bicara pelan-pelan supaya nenek bisa mendengar dengan jelas.
english: Please speak slowly so that Grandma can hear clearly.

target: Ibu memotong buah kecil-kecil supaya anak-anak mudah makan.
english: Mom cuts the fruit into small pieces so that the kids can eat it easily.
grammar: Doubled adjective = 'into pieces that size': potong kecil-kecil = cut into small pieces.

target: Simpan tiketmu di kantong depan tas supaya mudah diambil nanti.
english: Keep your ticket in the bag's front pocket so that it's easy to take out later.

target: Kami menabung setiap bulan supaya bisa membeli rumah kecil.
english: We save money every month so that we can buy a small house.

target: Saya menyalakan kipas angin supaya kamar tidak terlalu panas.
english: I turn on the fan so that the room doesn't get too hot.

target: Dia berolahraga tiga kali seminggu supaya badannya tetap sehat.
english: She exercises three times a week so that her body stays healthy.

target: Tutup pintunya rapat-rapat supaya nyamuk tidak masuk malam ini.
english: Close the door tightly so that mosquitoes don't get in tonight.
grammar: supaya tidak = so that ... not: supaya nyamuk tidak masuk = so the mosquitoes don't get in.

target: Mohon datang lima belas menit lebih awal agar acara mulai tepat waktu.
english: Please come fifteen minutes early so that the event starts on time.
grammar: agar = supaya in formal settings (announcements, notices): agar acara mulai tepat waktu. Say supaya in chat.

target: Tamu hotel diminta menunggu di lobi agar semuanya berjalan lancar.
english: Hotel guests are asked to wait in the lobby so that everything runs smoothly.

target: Matikan lampu ruang rapat agar kantor bisa hemat listrik.
english: Turn off the meeting room lights so that the office can save electricity.

target: Kirim laporanmu hari ini agar tim bisa membacanya sebelum rapat.
english: Send your report today so that the team can read it before the meeting.

target: Pengumuman itu dipasang di pintu agar semua karyawan segera tahu.
english: The announcement was put up on the door so that all employees would know right away.

target: Cuci tanganmu dengan sabun agar kuman tidak ikut masuk ke makanan.
english: Wash your hands with soap so that germs don't get into the food.

target: Meskipun hujan deras, pesta pernikahan itu tetap berjalan lancar.
english: Although it rained hard, the wedding party still went smoothly.
grammar: tetap = still/anyway after meskipun: Meskipun hujan, tetap berjalan = Although it rained, it still went ahead.

target: Meskipun sudah malam, toko kopi di sudut itu masih buka.
english: Although it's already late at night, the coffee shop on that corner is still open.
grammar: masih = still (ongoing now): masih buka = still open, masih hujan = still raining.

target: Meskipun harganya mahal, durian itu habis dalam satu jam.
english: Although the price was high, that durian was gone within an hour.

target: Meskipun lelah, ayah tetap menjemput kami di stasiun malam itu.
english: Although he was tired, Dad still picked us up at the station that night.

target: Meskipun kantornya jauh, dia tidak pernah datang terlambat.
english: Although his office is far away, he never arrives late.
grammar: No tapi after a meskipun clause: Meskipun jauh, dia datang — not 'tapi dia datang'.

target: Meskipun baru belajar setahun, bahasa Indonesianya sudah lancar sekali.
english: Although he has only studied for a year, his Indonesian is already very fluent.

target: Meskipun kamarnya kecil, hotel itu bersih dan dekat pantai.
english: Although the rooms are small, that hotel is clean and close to the beach.

target: Meskipun sedang diet, dia mencicipi kue buatan ibunya.
english: Although she is on a diet, she tasted the cake made by her mother.
grammar: buatan = made by: kue buatan ibunya = a cake made by her mother, buatan tangan = handmade.

target: Walaupun sudah tua, kakek masih berkebun setiap pagi di belakang rumah.
english: Although he is old, Grandpa still gardens every morning behind the house.
grammar: walaupun and meskipun both mean 'although' — swap freely: Walaupun tua = Meskipun tua = although (he's) old.

target: Walaupun jalannya jauh, kami memilih naik sepeda ke pasar.
english: Although the way is far, we choose to ride bikes to the market.

target: Walaupun gajinya lebih kecil, dia lebih suka pekerjaan barunya.
english: Although the salary is smaller, she prefers her new job.

target: Walaupun sudah minum obat, kepala saya masih pusing sampai sekarang.
english: Although I've taken medicine, my head is still dizzy even now.

target: Walaupun harus menunggu lama, kami tetap membeli tiket konser itu.
english: Although we had to wait a long time, we still bought the concert tickets.

target: Walaupun hari libur, ayah tetap membalas pesan dari kantornya.
english: Although it's a holiday, Dad still replies to messages from his office.

target: Walaupun masakan itu pedas sekali, turis itu menghabiskannya.
english: Although that dish was very spicy, the tourist finished all of it.
grammar: menghabiskan = to finish off: menghabiskannya = finished it (-nya = it).

target: Walaupun cuaca panas, anak-anak terus bermain bola di lapangan.
english: Although the weather is hot, the kids keep playing ball on the field.

target: Saya sudah mengetuk pintu dua kali, tetapi tidak ada jawaban.
english: I knocked on the door twice, but there was no answer.
grammar: tetapi = 'but' in careful or written style; in everyday talk say tapi: Mahal, tapi enak = Pricey, but tasty.

target: Kami ingin duduk di luar, tetapi semua meja sudah penuh.
english: We wanted to sit outside, but all the tables were already full.

target: Laporan itu sudah selesai, tetapi belum dikirim ke kantor pusat.
english: The report is finished, but it hasn't been sent to the head office yet.

target: Harga kamarnya murah, tetapi sarapannya tidak termasuk.
english: The room rate is cheap, but breakfast isn't included.
grammar: termasuk = included: sarapan tidak termasuk = breakfast not included — check this when booking.

target: Dia sudah tiba di bandara, tetapi pesawatnya tertunda dua jam.
english: He has arrived at the airport, but his plane is delayed by two hours.

target: Saya suka apartemen itu, tetapi jaraknya terlalu jauh dari kantor.
english: I like that apartment, but the distance to the office is too far.

target: Aku mau ikut ke pasar malam, tapi besok ada ujian.
english: I want to come along to the night market, but tomorrow there's an exam.
grammar: tapi is the everyday 'but' — fine in conversation: mau ikut, tapi ada ujian = want to come, but there's an exam.

target: Filmnya bagus, tapi kursi bioskopnya kurang nyaman.
english: The movie was good, but the cinema seats weren't very comfortable.

target: Saya sudah memanggil taksi, tapi mobilnya belum datang juga.
english: I've already called a taxi, but the car still hasn't come.
grammar: belum ... juga = STILL not: belum datang juga = still hasn't come (with impatience).

target: Kue ini enak, tapi terlalu manis untuk ayah saya.
english: This cake is tasty, but too sweet for my father.

target: Kami ingin berenang, tapi ombak sore ini besar sekali.
english: We want to swim, but the waves this afternoon are very big.

target: Dia rajin bekerja, tapi jarang mengambil cuti panjang.
english: He works hard, but rarely takes long leave.

target: Saya mencari sandal ukuran empat puluh, tapi warnanya tinggal hitam.
english: I'm looking for size forty sandals, but the only color left is black.
grammar: tinggal here = left/remaining: warnanya tinggal hitam = the only color left is black.

target: Rumah nenek jauh, tapi kami mengunjunginya setiap bulan.
english: Grandma's house is far away, but we visit her every month.

target: Tadi saya mampir ke tokomu, tapi pintunya sudah dikunci.
english: Earlier I stopped by your shop, but the door was already locked.

target: Bahasa Indonesianya belum lancar, tapi dia berani berbicara dengan siapa saja.
english: His Indonesian isn't fluent yet, but he dares to speak with anyone.

target: Hujan sudah berhenti, tapi jalan di depan rumah masih banjir.
english: The rain has stopped, but the road in front of the house is still flooded.

target: Ibu menyanyikan lagu lama sambil menjemur pakaian di halaman.
english: Mom sings an old song while hanging out the laundry in the yard.

target: Dia mendengarkan radio sambil menyetir ke kantor.
english: He listens to the radio while driving to the office.
grammar: sambil = while (one person, two actions at once): mendengarkan radio sambil menyetir = listen while driving.

target: Kami membahas rencana liburan sambil menunggu pesanan datang.
english: We discuss our holiday plans while waiting for our order to arrive.

target: Ayah minum kopi hitam sambil membaca koran pagi di teras.
english: Dad drinks black coffee while reading the morning paper on the porch.

target: Anak itu belajar berhitung sambil bermain kartu warna-warni.
english: That child learns to count while playing with colorful cards.

target: Saya menunggu bus sambil membalas pesan dari teman lama.
english: I wait for the bus while replying to messages from an old friend.

target: Mereka berjalan pelan-pelan di pantai sambil mencari kerang kecil.
english: They walk slowly along the beach while looking for little seashells.

target: Jangan main ponsel sambil menyeberang jalan, itu bahaya sekali.
english: Don't play on your phone while crossing the street; that's very dangerous.

target: Kakak memotong sayur sambil menonton acara masak di televisi.
english: Big sister chops vegetables while watching a cooking show on television.

target: Kami mengobrol santai sambil menikmati teh hangat di warung.
english: We chat casually while enjoying warm tea at the food stall.

target: Sebelum tamu datang, kami membersihkan ruang tamu bersama-sama.
english: Before the guests arrive, we clean the living room together.
grammar: sebelum can front a whole clause: Sebelum tamu datang, kami membersihkan = Before guests arrive, we clean.

target: Isi formulir ini sebelum namamu dipanggil di loket.
english: Fill in this form before your name is called at the counter.
grammar: di- = 'gets ...-ed': dipanggil = gets called, namamu dipanggil = your name is called.

target: Sebelum harga naik lagi, kami membeli tiket untuk liburan akhir tahun.
english: Before prices go up again, we're buying tickets for the year-end holiday.

target: Saya mengecek kompor dan jendela sebelum kami pergi berlibur.
english: I check the stove and the windows before we go on vacation.

target: Sebelum rapat dimulai, tolong bagikan laporan ini ke semua orang.
english: Before the meeting starts, please hand out this report to everyone.

target: Kami tiba di stasiun sebelum kereta pertama berangkat.
english: We arrived at the station before the first train departed.

target: Sebelum anak-anak bangun, ibu sudah menyiapkan sarapan di meja.
english: Before the kids wake up, Mom has already set out breakfast on the table.
grammar: No tense word after sebelum: sebelum anak-anak bangun covers 'before the kids wake / woke up'.

target: Sebelum hujan turun, angkat jemuran di halaman belakang, ya.
english: Before the rain comes down, bring in the laundry in the backyard, okay?
grammar: ya at the end softens a request: angkat jemuran, ya = bring in the laundry, okay?

target: Sebelum kamu tanda tangan, baca dulu semua halaman kontrak itu.
english: Before you sign, first read every page of that contract.

target: Sesudah hujan berhenti, kami melanjutkan perjalanan ke arah selatan.
english: After the rain stopped, we continued the journey southward.
grammar: sesudah = after; setelah means the same: Sesudah hujan berhenti = After the rain stopped.

target: Sesudah tamu terakhir pulang, kami mencuci semua piring kotor.
english: After the last guest went home, we washed all the dirty dishes.

target: Sesudah dia lulus kuliah, dia langsung bekerja di bank daerah.
english: After he graduated from college, he went straight to work at a local bank.

target: Sesudah kamu mencoba baju itu, gantung lagi di tempatnya, ya.
english: After you try on that dress, hang it back in its place, okay?

target: Sesudah pesawat mendarat, kami langsung mencari taksi ke hotel.
english: After the plane landed, we immediately looked for a taxi to the hotel.

target: Sesudah makan malam selesai, ayah mencuci piring dan saya mengeringkannya.
english: After dinner is over, Dad washes the dishes and I dry them.

target: Sesudah obatnya habis, jangan lupa kembali ke klinik lagi.
english: After the medicine runs out, don't forget to come back to the clinic.

target: Sesudah kelas selesai, kami mengobrol dalam bahasa Indonesia di kantin.
english: After class ends, we chat in Indonesian in the canteen.

target: Sesudah gajian, dia selalu mengajak keluarganya makan di luar.
english: After payday, he always takes his family out to eat.
grammar: gajian = payday (from gaji, salary): sesudah gajian = after payday.

target: Berangkat sekarang, kalau tidak kita ketinggalan kereta pagi.
english: Leave now; otherwise we'll miss the morning train.
grammar: kalau tidak = otherwise (literally 'if not'): kalau tidak, kita ketinggalan kereta = otherwise we miss the train.

target: Tulis alamatnya sekarang, kalau tidak kamu pasti lupa lagi.
english: Write down the address now; otherwise you'll definitely forget again.

target: Simpan kue itu di kulkas, kalau tidak semut datang.
english: Put that cake in the fridge; otherwise the ants will come.

target: Pakai topi dan kacamata hitam, kalau tidak kepalamu kepanasan.
english: Wear a hat and sunglasses; otherwise your head will get overheated.

target: Kita harus memesan meja dulu, kalau tidak restorannya pasti penuh.
english: We have to reserve a table first; otherwise the restaurant will definitely be full.

target: Kerjakan tugasmu malam ini, kalau tidak besok kamu akan repot.
english: Do your assignment tonight; otherwise tomorrow you'll be in trouble.

target: Bawa jaket tebal ke gunung, kalau tidak kamu kedinginan malam hari.
english: Bring a thick jacket to the mountain; otherwise you'll be freezing at night.
grammar: ke-...-an = badly affected by: kedinginan = freezing cold, kehujanan = caught in the rain.

target: Catat semua pengeluaranmu, kalau tidak uang gajimu cepat habis.
english: Write down all your expenses; otherwise your salary will run out fast.

target: Karena besok ada rapat penting, saya menyiapkan bahannya malam ini.
english: Because there's an important meeting tomorrow, I'm preparing the materials tonight.

target: Dia bekerja sambil kuliah, jadi waktunya untuk istirahat sedikit sekali.
english: He works while going to college, so he has very little time to rest.

target: Kalau kamu lelah, istirahat dulu sebelum kita melanjutkan latihan ini.
english: If you're tired, rest first before we continue this practice.

target: Meskipun sudah larut, dia menunggu di bandara supaya bisa menjemput tamunya.
english: Although it was late, he waited at the airport so that he could pick up his guest.

target: Saya membawa kamus kecil, jadi saya bisa membaca menu walaupun tidak ada gambarnya.
english: I brought a small dictionary, so I can read the menu even though there are no pictures.
grammar: walaupun can sit mid-sentence: bisa membaca walaupun tidak ada gambar = can read even though no pictures.

target: Tanya dulu harganya sebelum kamu membayar, soalnya di pasar bisa tawar-menawar.
english: Ask the price first before you pay, because at the market you can haggle.
grammar: tawar-menawar = haggling (back-and-forth doubling): bisa tawar-menawar = you can bargain.

target: Kami berangkat sebelum matahari terbit supaya tiba di puncak sebelum siang.
english: We set off before sunrise so that we'd reach the peak before midday.
